summary: Tenant routing hold during canary health-probe snooze prevents fallback and leaves traffic stuck
description:
Issue summary: Several HelixCare tenants observed sustained routing 'hold' during a canary rollout window where their explicit model pin did not commit and traffic did not fall back to the configured secondary variant. The control plane reported the canary cohort as in 'snoozed' health-probe state and suppressed fallback behavior.

Impact: Customer-facing production requests were routed to a single degraded canary pod for ~18 minutes, causing increased latency (p50 -> ~1.2s to 2.8s) and some 5xx spike for streamed sessions. Estimated ~0.6% error uplift across the customer's traffic during the window.

Observed behavior: - Orchestrator logs show cohort marked as "probe_snooze" which sets a local flag suppressing automatic fallback. - Pin commit handshake never progressed from PREPARE -> COMMIT for affected tenants. - Edge continued to route to the canary cohort due to sticky route lease being extended by the snooze path. - Manual force-commit restored normal routing.

Initial timeline: 2026-03-12T09:04 UTC - HelixCare first reported increased tail-latency. 2026-03-12T09:08 UTC - #support Slack pinged and ticket opened. 2026-03-12T09:22 UTC - On-call engaged; preliminary mitigation applied (manually force-commit pin). 2026-03-12T09:42 UTC - Observed routing normalized, metrics returned to baseline.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) On a dedicated cluster with an active canary (weight 5%) enable health-probe-snooze feature flag on orchestrator config for a short window.
2) Trigger a gradual rollout that requires pin commit for tenant affinity.
3) Simulate canary pod health flapping to cause orchestrator to mark cohort with probe_snooze.
4) Observe that tenants with explicit version pin remain routed to canary and fallback logic is suppressed until manual intervention.

investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered: 1) Orchestrator's health-probe snooze path is setting a suppression flag that also prevents fallback triggers — this is expected for short probe windows, but a race occurs when pin handshake times out while snooze is active. 2) Edge sticky-lease extension logic did not honor pin-handshake ABORT and kept tenant affinity to canary. 3) A recent config roll (orchestrator PR #589) modified the probe_snooze TTL behavior and may not have backoff for handshake aborts.

Findings: - Confirmed a code path in orchestrator where probe_snooze sets fallback_enabled=false for the cohort. If pin-handshake remains in PREPARE and then times out, fallback_enabled is not re-enabled until the cohort exits snooze. That window can exceed handshake timeout causing tenants to be stranded. - Edge lease extension uses cohort.snooze_ttl to extend session affinity; combined this held traffic on canary. - Reproduced locally with a simulated TTL of 15s and handshake artificial delay -> routing hold reproduced consistently.

Metrics checked: - routing.affinity.held_count increased by tenant. - controlplane.handshake.timeouts spike at same time. - Serving runtime logs showed increased queue depth on canary pods.

resolution:
Mitigation applied: manual force-commit of pin for affected tenants and rolling restart of the canary-coordinator process to clear snooze flags.
Permanent fix plan: 1) Patch orchestrator to ensure probe_snooze does not permanently suppress fallback when a pin handshake aborts (PR to add explicit re-enable on ABORT). 2) Add safe-guard: edge should not extend sticky-lease beyond max_handshake_timeout when cohort is in a transient snooze state. 3) Add synthetic regression test exercising PREPARE -> TIMEOUT while probe_snooze active.
Rollout notes: Patch PR target branch release/2.8.1. Expect to ship hotfix within 72 hours pending review.
